subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): bound auth-profile JSON reads with size cap

question: Should OpenClaw make 10 MiB the supported maximum for persisted auth-profile JSON and retain the current silent “no credential source” recovery behavior for oversized existing stores?
rationale: The code can enforce either policy, but choosing a permanent cap and user recovery behavior changes the compatibility contract for persisted authentication data and requires maintainer product judgment.

options.title: Accept the 10 MiB cap
options.body: Merge the bounded reader with the existing null-return recovery path, treating auth-profile stores as compact configuration files.

options.title: Add explicit oversized-store recovery
options.body: Keep the bounded reader but provide a supported diagnostic or Doctor-guided path that distinguishes an oversized store from missing credentials.

options.title: Pause the cap change
options.body: Keep the current behavior until maintainers select a size threshold and recovery contract backed by auth-store usage evidence.

recommendation.title: Add explicit oversized-store recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded reader but provide a supported diagnostic or Doctor-guided path that distinguishes an oversized store from missing credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the most direct implementation context in the supplied history, though a current-main auth-profile owner should make the final contract decision.
